extractions.quote:
Introduction
Stiff-person syndrome (SPS), first described by Moersch and Woltman in 1956 [1], typically presents between the 3rd and 6th decade of life and is manifested by fluctuating rigidity of axial musculature with painful episodic simultaneous co -contraction of agonist and antagonist muscles. Episodes may be triggered by tactile, emotional, or auditory stimuli. Comorbid anxiety may be present which may raise suspicion of a psychogenic disorder and delay diagnosis [2]. Antibodies against glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD), gamma-amino butyric acid A receptor-associated protein, and amphiphysin I have been identified in this disorder [2, 3].
